subject: Feature asks prioritization: HealthSpring audit + BYOK exception
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Feature asks prioritization: HealthSpring audit + BYOK exception

Team — quick context and request: HealthSpring (Evan Morales) surfaced a commercial gating ask during legal/procurement; they need clarity on three items before signing:

1) Audit log export and retention: they want a 3-year retention export capability for SSO and API audit trails, plus an easy handoff format for their auditors.
2) BYOK exception: their architecture requires short-lived customer-managed keys for debug/forensics. They are asking if we can allow a 30-day retention window for ephemeral CMKs (temporary escrow) on a per-customer exception basis.
3) Evidence packaging: procurement wants a one-pager for compliance that explains what artifacts we can deliver (log schema, access logs, Keystore handoff steps).

This is a cross-functional triage. Naomi — can you categorize these as Must/Backlog/Exception and call out any blocking controls (SOC2 scope, legal review)? Marcus — estimate effort to produce an export pipeline/stable schema + rough time for an opt-in temporary-escrow flow. Marissa — call out product tradeoffs and whether this needs a roadmap slot or can be handled as a patch. Ben — FYI from the deal side: timeline is ~3 weeks (procurement pressure).

I attached the HealthSpring evidence request and their procurement note. Can we get a short decision today so Ben can push back/submit the options?

Thanks,
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
PM, Security & Compliance Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature asks prioritization: HealthSpring audit + BYOK exception

Thanks for the summary, Jasmine. Quick triage notes below (high level):

- Audit export/3yr retention: Must-have for customer evaluation but not necessarily a platform-wide default. We can support long-term retention via scheduled export to customer-controlled storage (S3/GCS) and a packaged evidence bundle. Blocking items: current export tooling only supports 90-day rolling snapshots for hosted customers; extending to 3yr requires storage/export orchestration + legal approval re: our retention posture in hosted vs private deployments.

- BYOK ephemeral 30-day escrow (exception): This is an exception to our default of no customer-key escrow. Technically possible if we: (a) accept a customer-provided key into a temporary escrow vault, (b) run a short retention window (30 days) with tight audit for access, (c) require an approved security exception ticket and legal signoff. Blockers: KMS policy changes (key lifecycle APIs), SOC2 evidence implications (we must document procedural controls), product telemetry to ensure we can surface access.

- Evidence one-pager: straightforward; can be produced by RD + security. Suggest: a short matrix showing deliverable (audit logs, auth flows, keystore handshake), format (JSON/CSV), typical SLA for export, and ownership.

I propose the following buckets (for Ben to present to HealthSpring):
  * Option A (Enterprise): Dedicated evidence export + 3yr customer archive (Recommended; needs 6-8w ops+legal)
  * Option B (Temporary Exception): 30-day ephemeral-key escrow + 90-day audit export (Fast-track; needs security exception and 2-3w engineering)
  * Option C (Workaround): Customer pulls live exports via API + self-manages long-term retention (Immediate; limited for audits)

I'll draft a security exception template and open SEC-4521 with the details. Marcus — I need a quick note from you on engineering feasibility for Option B (2-3w estimate) so I can include both technical and control mitigations.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature asks prioritization: HealthSpring audit + BYOK exception

Looping in engineering constraints and rough plan.

Notes:
- Export pipeline: we already have an internal job that materializes logs to parquet for short windows. Extending to a packaged long-term export involves: export orchestration (1w), schema stabilization (2-3d), secure transfer to customer (s3 presigned or transfer job) (2d), QA (3d). End-to-end for Option A (full 3yr plan) is ~6w if we include infra quotas and storage costs.

- Temporary key escrow (Option B): doable as a scoped feature if we restrict to Dedicated and Private deployments first — hosted customers present compliance/legal complexity. Implementation outline: a temporary escrow store that accepts CMK metadata but we do NOT replicate raw key material; instead we record wrapped key references and an audit trail; retention TTL enforcement is automated. Estimated implementation: 2-3w for the minimal flow (secure vault + TTL + audit hooks) assuming no upstream KMS provider changes. If we need HSM-backed escrow or cross-region replication, add 2-4w.

- Risks: Key escrow increases compliance burden; we must ensure no persistent raw key exposure and strict role separation. Audit trail size could be large for SSO auth flows — recommend compressing exports and including an index for fast lookups.

I will create a spike branch and a short RFC by EOD to capture wireframes and the infra checklist (link SEC-4521). If we go the Exception path, we should limit to a single pilot customer and add a postmortem requirement.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff Engineer, Infra
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature asks prioritization: HealthSpring audit + BYOK exception

Appreciate the quick triage. A couple of commercial notes from my side:

- Procurement pushed for the 3-week signature timeline. If we offer Option B (Temporary Exception) with a dated expiration and an explicit security exception, they will likely accept that as a near-term path.
- HealthSpring asked for a short procurement-ready factsheet that summarizes: what we deliver, what they must do (e.g., where to store exports), and the signoff required (security + legal). Can Marissa own a one-pager? If we can produce that by Mon AM, I can send it to Evan and procurement and buy the team a week.
- There is a potential ask for a small onboarding credit linked to the exception (they requested a 10% onboarding credit). I don't want to approve that without leadership, but flagging it since timelines could hinge on commercial flexibility.

If we can commit to Option B timeline (2-3w) and a security exception template, I'll push for the exception route.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evan Morales <evan@healthspring.com>, HealthSpring Compliance <compliance@healthspring.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature asks prioritization: HealthSpring audit + BYOK exception

Thanks everyone — summary & next steps (agreed):

Decision: pursue Option B (Temporary Exception) as a near-term path to unblock procurement. We will pilot with HealthSpring and explicitly limit to Dedicated/Private customers for the initial rollout.

Action items:
- Naomi: draft security exception template + control mitigations and open SEC-4521 (ETA: EOD today).
- Marcus: RFC + spike branch for the temporary escrow flow; include TTL enforcement, audit hooks, and minimal QA checklist (ETA: 2-3w).
- Marissa: create the procurement factsheet (one-pager) and the export matrix doc (ETA: Mon 09:00 PT). Attachments: I've uploaded the procurement note and the proposed retention matrix.
- Ben: communicate Option B to HealthSpring; request procurement to sign the exception acknowledgement and defer longer-term export work to roadmap.

I'll follow up with a short public note for Leadership and copy Legal once Naomi has the exception draft. If any blocker appears (legal/KMS vendor limitation), escalate to Marcus and Naomi immediately.

Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
PM, Security & Compliance Integrations
Redwood Inference
